title: Timer version label behind a warning or a breach
source: RWB-E1-028 BR9 and section 13; FSD P7 A2.3; TSD P7 T3.1
description: The legacy story requires every timer start, warning and breach to be logged with its rule and version, and decision_log_entry.rule_version holds 20 characters, but no source names the rule ID or the version scheme of a service-level timer. The story writes the placeholder of section 8 and does not invent a label such as SLA-2026.11.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-028 BR9 and section 13 (no label given); TSD P7 T3.1 DF-DEC-004 and DF-DEC-005 (varchar(20)); FSD P7 A2.3; Temporal and Drools design slide 16 (only rule package labels such as ALLOC-2026.12 are exemplified)
proposed: Name the timer rule ID and its version scheme with the SERVICE_LEVEL parameters of rwb-case, then replace the placeholder in section 8 and in the writer's shape check

title: No field and no decision code for a timer decision
source: TSD P7 T3.1; FSD P7 A2.14.3.2; RWB-E1-028 AC2
description: A breach entry must carry the escalation role and the escalation level, and every entry carries a decision_code from LOV-DECISION, whose values are D5.1 to D9.3, X1 to X7 or an access event. TSD P7 T3.1 has no column for an escalation role or a level, and LOV-DECISION has no timer value. The story carries the two values in actions (DF-DEC-014) and takes the decision code the writer fixes.
evidence: TSD P7 T3.1 decision_log_entry (no escalation role or level column); FSD P7 A2.14.3.2 (decision_code LOV-DECISION values); legacy RWB-E1-028 AC2 (escalation level 1, escalation role RW-TEAMMGR)
proposed: Add the timer decision codes to LOV-DECISION and fix either a column pair or a documented actions payload in RWB-P7-E1008-APP and RWB-P7-E1027-APP, then replace the assumption in this story

title: Order of the case read: decided_at or chain_seq
source: FSD P3 A2.37; legacy RWB-E2-005; this work package
description: This story fixes the case read of the ledger in decided_at order, while FSD P3 A2.37 and legacy RWB-E2-005 fix chain_seq order. A record decided earlier can be appended later, so the two orders differ and an auditor reads a different sequence under each. The story returns decided_at order and carries chainSeq on every item so both orders are visible.
evidence: FSD P3 AC-P3-037-01 and AC-ALT-P3-037-01 (entries return in chain_seq order); legacy RWB-E2-005 steps 3 and 4 (query and paging in chain_seq order); this work package (decided_at order)
proposed: Keep chain_seq order as the ledger order and decided_at as a sort the screen may apply, or declare both on DecisionLogPage; settle it in RWB-P7-E2005-APP and align this story's AC3
